THE ARCH IS BACK — four ways to modernize it
Same mihrab silhouette and the same real data in all four; what changes is the fill. The semicircular top is the original CSS trick (a radius of exactly half the width), so it stays a true semicircle at any size.
The khatim star at the crown is drawn in SVG — it replaces the low-res logo.png crop the old arch used.

A · Solid arch (refined)
What you had: green fill, one gold hairline following the arc. Modernized by softening the bottom corners, redrawing the mark, and giving the data a real type hierarchy (gold year eyebrow, cream label, gold values).
Tradeoff: two large dark shapes still sit heavily on the page — it is the least changed and the least airy.

B · Light arch
Inverts the weight: a warm white card with a gold outline, and only the dome stays green to carry the heading. Green ink on light, so the numbers read much more sharply.
Tradeoff: the page already gained light cards elsewhere — this makes the arch quieter, and it no longer anchors the section the way a dark shape does.

C · Outline arch
No fill at all — a single gold line on the bare page, so the ground texture runs straight through the arch. Roman numerals and prices in green ink, generous space.
Tradeoff: the most modern and the most fragile. With this much air the two arches need to be near-equal in content or the emptier one looks unfinished.

D · Gold crown
The dome is struck in gold with the heading in deep green, over a green body. The most graphic of the four and the closest to an illuminated manuscript headpiece.
Tradeoff: gold is doing a lot of work here. It will fight the gold in the divider medallions and the hero kicker unless those are toned down.
